items.word: The politician was quick to disavow the controversial statements.
items.definition:
disavow
to deny any responsibility or support for

items.word: His constant failures began to embitter him.
items.definition:
embitter
to make someone feel bitter or resentful

items.word: The cult tried to indoctrinate new members with its ideology.
items.definition:
indoctrinate
teach (a person or group) to accept a set of beliefs uncritically

items.word: The law proscribes the use of certain chemicals in food production.
items.definition:
proscribe
to forbid or prohibit

items.word: The lawyer tried to rebut the witness's testimony.
items.definition:
rebut
to prove (a statement or charge) to be false

items.word: He sought to unencumber himself from all his worldly possessions.
items.definition:
unencumber
to free from a burden or impediment

items.word: It's wrong to denigrate someone's efforts without understanding their challenges.
items.definition:
denigrate
criticize unfairly; disparage

items.word: It took a long time to extricate the car from the mud.
items.definition:
extricate
free (someone or something) from a difficulty or constraint

items.word: Verbs in English do not inflect as much as in other languages.
items.definition:
inflect
to change the form of a word to express a grammatical function

items.word: In the forest, oak trees tend to predominate over other species.
items.definition:
predominate
be the strongest or main element; be greater in number or amount

items.word: The software needs to serialize the data before saving it.
items.definition:
serialize
to arrange in a series or sequence

items.word: The government was forced to accede to the protesters' demands.
items.definition:
accede
to agree to a demand, request, or treaty

items.word: He tried to bluster his way out of trouble.
items.definition:
bluster
talk in a loud, aggressive, or arrogant way

items.word: Many countries have chosen to criminalize certain drugs.
items.definition:
criminalize
To make something illegal.

items.word: Some companies were accused of trying to profiteer during the crisis.
items.definition:
profiteer
make or seek to make an excessive or unfair profit

items.word: A good meal will sate your hunger.
items.definition:
sate
satisfy (a desire or an appetite) to the full

items.word: I don't begrudge him his success.
items.definition:
begrudge
to envy someone the possession or enjoyment of something

items.word: He tried to eschew all forms of luxury.
items.definition:
eschew
deliberately avoid using; abstain from

items.word: Doctors inoculate children against various diseases.
items.definition:
inoculate
to treat (a person or animal) with a vaccine to produce immunity against a disease

items.word: A warm glow began to suffuse the room as the sun set.
items.definition:
suffuse
spread through or over

items.word: The sensor actuates the alarm when motion is detected.
items.definition:
actuate
to cause (a machine or device) to operate

items.word: The complex instructions began to addle his brain.
items.definition:
addle
to confuse or muddle (someone's mind)

items.word: Steps were taken to ameliorate the living conditions of the refugees.
items.definition:
ameliorate
to make (something bad or unsatisfactory) better

items.word: The complex instructions left him completely bemused.
items.definition:
bemuse
Puzzle, confuse, or bewilder.

items.word: He used a soft cloth to burnish the silver.
items.definition:
burnish
Polish (something, especially metal) by rubbing.

items.word: The challenger hoped to dethrone the reigning champion.
items.definition:
dethrone
Remove from a position of power or authority.

items.word: Ancient Egyptians would embalm their pharaohs.
items.definition:
embalm
To preserve a body from decay

items.word: There were no circumstances to extenuate his actions.
items.definition:
extenuate
To make (guilt or an offense) seem less serious or more forgivable

items.word: The baby started to grizzle when he couldn't reach his toy.
items.definition:
grizzle
to complain or cry fretfully

items.word: The judge will mete out justice to the criminals.
items.definition:
mete
To dispense or allot justice, punishment, or harsh treatment.

items.word: Don't misconstrue my silence as disapproval.
items.definition:
misconstrue
To interpret (something, especially a person's words or actions) wrongly.

items.word: Some believe that our destiny is preordained by a higher power.
items.definition:
preordain
to decide or determine beforehand; to destine

items.word: She was beguiled by his charming smile.
items.definition:
beguile
to charm or enchant someone, sometimes in a deceptive way

items.word: The literary critic sought to deconstruct the novel's themes.
items.definition:
deconstruct
to analyze or break down (a text or concept) into its component parts

items.word: He would often ejaculate a witty remark during the meeting.
items.definition:
ejaculate
to utter suddenly; to expel semen

items.word: The urgency of the situation helped to galvanise the team into action.
items.definition:
galvanise
to shock or excite (someone) into taking action; to coat (iron or steel) with a protective layer of zinc
